result:
`final.py` scores **0.559 on the search split, against 0.365 for the LRU baseline**. I used **11 of the 24 scorer calls**, including the last one, which confirmed `final.py` is valid.

**What it does:**
- **Core policy:** W-TinyLFU. New keys go into a small LRU "window". When one leaves the window, it only enters the main cache if it has been requested more often than the key it would push out. The main cache is split into a probation section and a protected section.
- **Self-tuning:** 18 small shadow caches try different settings. Each one sees a hashed 1/8 sample of the keys and has 1/8 of the capacity. Together they cover 6 window sizes (1%–85%) and 3 rates of forgetting old request counts. The real cache switches to whichever setting has had the most recent hits. This beat both fixed settings and Caffeine-style hill climbing.

| trace | LRU | final |
|---|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.175 | 0.248 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.227 | 0.662 |
| phases | 0.619 | 0.640 |
| mixed | 0.158 | 0.266 |
| recency | 0.848 | 0.843 |
| shifting_loops | 0.164 | 0.698 |

**How I got there on the scorer:** plain W-TinyLFU scored 0.503. Adding the hill-climbed window gave 0.523, and shadow caches choosing the window size gave about 0.546. Letting the shadows also choose how fast old counts fade gave about 0.56.

**Things to know:**
- **Hidden traces:** the last few variants scored 0.553–0.560, mostly because `shifting_loops` moves between 0.67 and 0.71. Expect roughly 0.55–0.56 on the unseen traces rather than exactly 0.559.
- **Recency trace:** it's the one place the final cache trails LRU, and only slightly.
- **Speed:** it took about 0.2 s per 50,000 requests on this machine, so it should fit well within the 8 s limit. The scorer doesn't report time, so I couldn't confirm that on the real traces.

I tuned the settings on my own synthetic traces, which are modelled on the six trace names, to save scorer calls. My test scripts are in `/tmp/ck`, outside the task folder. I left my intermediate candidate files (`wtlfu.py`, `adapt.py`, `shadow*.py`, `s_*.py`, `sh2*.py`) in the task folder alongside `final.py`.
